title: Flooding
label: FLOOD
deck: Distance from floodwater is the first safety decision.
tldr: Move to higher ground if water is rising or a flash-flood warning affects you. Never walk, swim, or drive through floodwater; depth, current, contamination, and road damage are hard to judge. Follow evacuation orders and avoid basements or low areas that can fill rapidly.
steps: Leave low ground and move to a safe higher location. If a road is flooded, turn around and choose another route.
Check alerts, road closures, and evacuation instructions. Do not rely on the road being open because it was open earlier.
Floodwater may hide energized wires, debris, sewage, chemicals, and missing road surface. Keep children and pets away.
Give your precise location to emergency services. Move to a higher level if possible; avoid entering a closed attic where you could become trapped by rising water.
next: Return only when officials say it is safe. Photograph damage without entering unstable structures, use protective gear for cleanup, and check the water supply for advisories.
watch: Flooding can begin far from the heaviest rain. Do not attempt to cross flowing water to reach a vehicle, home, or belongings.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Identify higher ground reachable without crossing water. Pack essentials while routes remain dry; if they are already cut off, use the safest elevated space available and signal for help. Stay out of a basement that is taking on water.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
